chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abī Wallād al-Ḥannāṭ, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought two men, each of whom had accused the other of zina in his body. He said: so he averted the hadd punishment from them both and administered taʿzir to them.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام as the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse; the accusation concerned this offense
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: the fixed legal punishment prescribed for certain crimes
key_terms.بِرَجُلَيْنِ: with two men brought before the Imam for judgment
key_terms.عَزَّرَهُمَا: he administered discretionary punishment to both of them
key_terms.قَذَفَ: to accuse someone of illicit sexual misconduct

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام when two people accused each other of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal judgment of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning two men who mutually accused one another of zina. The hadd punishment was not applied, but both were given taʿzir, indicating a discretionary punishment in a case of mutual defamatory accusation.
